unreg:season_stat_feats#sstat_rules_not_.rationale: Only the velocity KXMLBSTAT event is in the sampled rules file; for the eight feats only a one-sentence API wording exists and no text defines a no-hitter, perfect game, distance rounding or suspended games, so only a Kalshi rule document or settled examples can close it.

unreg:season_stat_feats#sstat_p105_unret.rationale: The events listing shows KXMLBSTAT-26P105 but both the nested markets and the markets endpoint returned nothing for it on 2026-11-09, so its wording cannot be retrieved from the public API from here.

unreg:season_stat_feats#sstat_distance_t.rationale: The 500-foot tail input is defined with a generalised-Pareto fit and a shape sensitivity; how many Statcast home runs sit at or beyond 500 feet and how stable the fitted tail is are empirical questions to be answered by counting and fitting Savant data.

unreg:season_stat_feats#sstat_rate_stabi.rationale: The hazard input is defined as a Poisson-rate regression on league covariates; whether those rates are stable across eras and overdispersed relative to Poisson is a backtest on 1990-2025 league-season counts, not missing catalog content.

unreg:season_stat_feats#sstat_scope_resi.rationale: Future seasons may add or rename KXMLBSTAT events; the eleven events listed on 2026-11-09 are mapped, and new ones can only be routed when they are listed in a later season.

unreg:player_home_run_exposure#hrx_misse.rationale: Neither sampled text covers an injured, benched or traded player or the inclusion of postseason games in a window; only full Kalshi rules or settled examples can settle that reading.

unreg:player_home_run_exposure#hrx_sampl.rationale: Only one rung and one window were sampled per series; other rungs, series and windows can be sampled when further markets are captured, and the archetype inputs do not depend on the missing variants.

unreg:player_home_run_exposure#hrx_dispe.rationale: The shared game-level dispersion of home runs is a parameter to fit on 2015-2025 player-game counts and test on series totals; the dispersion input is already defined in the postseason-count archetype and the per-PA model carries a placeholder.

unreg:player_home_run_exposure#hrx_pitch.rationale: Whether opposing managers pitch around top power hitters more in the postseason is measurable from intentional-walk and non-swing rates in historical playoff games; it is an effect size to estimate, not missing catalog structure.

unreg:pitcher_scoreless_innings_streak#s.rationale: KXMLBSISTREAK does not say whether unearned or inherited-runner runs or relief outs break or count towards the streak; only Kalshi rule text or a settled example can fix the reading, and the ledger input keeps both.
The text does not state how an injured-list stint, role change or trade settles; it is a settlement reading only the exchange can supply.

How hard to regress observed scoreless rates for a pitcher already on a streak is a shrinkage constant to backtest on all 30+ inning streaks since 1990; the survival and luck-regression inputs are defined.
Whether the exchange's displayed streak total matches a play-by-play reconstruction can only be checked by capturing the exchange's value for several pitchers and dates in the future.

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.rationale: Re-homed pointer: the streak-break reading concerns KXMLBSISTREAK, now in pitcher_scoreless_innings_streak (sis_break_definition); only Kalshi rules or a settled example can settle it.
Re-homed pointer: missed-game settlement concerns KXMLBSERIESHR and KXMLBNEXTHR, now in player_home_run_exposure (hrx_missed_games_settlement); only Kalshi rules or settled examples can settle it.

Re-homed pointer: the streak-persistence shrinkage concerns KXMLBSISTREAK, now in pitcher_scoreless_innings_streak (sis_streak_persistence), and is a backtest constant rather than missing catalog content.

unreg:season_stat_feats#sstat_no_hitter_.rationale: The rule text and event title disagree on whether a combined no-hitter counts; the hazard input carries both branches, so only a Kalshi rule document or a settled example can fix which reading settles the market.

unreg:player_home_run_exposure#hrx_windo.rationale: Whether All-Star Game home runs inside the window count and how the boundary dates are read are not stated in the sampled text; only the exchange can clarify, and the window input counts team games from the official schedule either way.

unreg:pitcher_scoreless_innings_streak#s.rationale: Which public feed exposes run responsibility and inherited-runner attribution, and whether an official scoring-correction window exists, were not checked from here; the ledger input is defined and needs an inspection of the feeds to confirm availability.

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_thres.rationale: Where 105, 106 and 107 mph sit relative to the tracked record is countable from Savant pitch data and the threshold-parametrised extreme-value input is already defined; the counts and the tail fit are empirical work, not missing catalog structure.

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes#velo_feed_.rationale: Intermediate live-feed readings that were later removed are not archived publicly, so the anomaly rate cannot be measured from available data; the capture design is in the input definition.

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials#.rationale: The best-of-3 Wild Card round exists only in recent postseasons, so its calibration data accumulate over future seasons; the format table can be checked against MLB documentation but the history cannot be extended.
